newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek court acquits Moslem journalist.
newsitem.headline: Greek court acquits Moslem journalist.

text.p: The publisher of a Turkish-language newspaper in northern Greece was acquitted on Thursday in a case that had drawn protests from human rights and media groups.

Abdulhalim Dede of the weekly Trakyanin Sesi (Thracian Voice) was changed over an article he wrote alleging that local authorities were conniving in a campaign to thwart community projects for the Moslem minority.
He was accused of "spreading false information that may cause public unrest or shake people's faith in the Greek state".
A court official in the town of Komotini near the Greek-Turkish border told Reuters the one-day trial ended with an acquittal.
Media watchdog groups described the case as an attempt to muzzle a prominent voice in Greece's 130,000-strong Moslem minority.
The Greek office of the Helsinki Watch human rights group campaigned to have the charges dropped.

The Foreign Press Association of Greece sent a defence witness to the court and said in a statement that Dede, who has been a stringer for Agence France Presse since 1987, "has always been a very careful journalist driven only by his passion for the truth".
"By prosecuting me they are trying to terrorise Moslems in Western Thrace," Dede told Reuters before the trial.
Athens says there is no such thing in Greece as an ethnic Turkish minority but a Moslem community of various ethnic backgrounds, remnants of the Ottoman Empire which ruled the area until 1913.
Ankara says Thrace's Moslems are Turks and their minority rights are violated by the Greek government.
